mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous quarter -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that elevates wage inflation and input costs, compressing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% over three months signals a shift from spending to saving, implying lower near-term demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous quarter +2% AND GDPC1 < previous quarter -1% over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) cut below 2% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%) signals an accommodative policy stance that supports risk assets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month +5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
